pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:336 Jobs found `running` at boot, at lease expiry or at the drain deadline are closed through the ordinary `fail` door with only a prose reason (FailReason::Text sets no cause_kind). With attempts used up they become `Failed`, and JobStatus has no indeterminate value, so 'outcome unknown' is stored as a definite failure that consumers can only recover by reading the message text.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1853 The recovery sweep writes FAILURE (requeue, or Failed once attempts run out) instead of a first-class indeterminate status. The verdict lives only in the error string; the core test at crates/core/tests/jobs.rs:323 recovers it with `contains("lease expired")`, which is the technique's named tell.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path assigns the job record's status vocabulary to job-coordination, while this technique requires a third, indeterminate status. A scrape-job queue that hosts no agent loop sits between the two. The registry should say which subject owns the interrupted-job status when the job is not an agent tool call.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/e2e/panic_containment.rs:60 The API-contract e2e suite pins that a panic is told apart from an app error, a timeout or a reaped lease by the error message prefix alone (all of them end as `Failed`), so the contract it guards is a verdict held in prose rather than in status or cause_kind.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/e2e/panic_containment.rs:60 The test separates panic from the reaper's 'lease expired (heartbeat stale)' label by string comparison, which is the technique's 'string comparison against an error message' tell.
